t.6.76.1: Then Dāśarathi, tormentor of his foes, having fitted an arrow to his bow, released it at the lord of the Rākṣasas, enraged and hissing like a serpent.
t.6.76.2: Hearing the resounding twang of his bowstring against the arm-guard, the son of Rāvaṇa turned pale in the face and gazed at Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.76.3: Seeing that rākṣasa, the son of Rāvaṇa, with a dejected face, Vibhīṣaṇa spoke to Saumitri, who was engaged in battle.
t.6.76.4: Judging by the signs I observe in this son of Rāvaṇa, he is broken, there is no doubt; therefore make haste, O mighty-armed one.
t.6.76.5: Then Saumitri fitted his arrows, which were like tongues of flame, and loosed them all at him, sharpened and as if virulent with poison.
t.6.76.6: Struck by Lakṣmaṇa with arrows whose touch was like Śakra's thunderbolt, he became stupefied for a moment, all his senses thrown into turmoil.
t.6.76.7: After a moment, regaining consciousness with his senses restored, the hero saw the heroic son of Daśaratha standing firm before him.
t.6.76.8: With his eyes reddened by rage, he advanced upon Saumitri, and, having come up to him, he once again addressed him with harsh words.
t.6.76.9: Do you not remember my prowess in that first battle, when you, bound together with your brother, lay writhing on the battlefield?
t.6.76.10: Indeed, in the great battle, you two youths were first laid upon the ground by arrows like Śakra's thunderbolt, lying senseless together with your foremost followers.
t.6.76.11: Either you have lost your memory, I think, or clearly you wish to go to the abode of Yama, since you wish to assail me.
t.6.76.12: If my prowess was not seen by you in the first battle, today I shall show it to you; now stand firm where you are.
t.6.76.13: Having spoken thus, he pierced Lakṣmaṇa with seven arrows, and Hanūmān with ten excellent shafts of sharp edge.
t.6.76.14: Then the valiant one, doubly enraged out of wrath, pierced Vibhīṣaṇa with a hundred well-aimed arrows.
t.6.76.15: Then Rāma's younger brother, having seen that deed done by Indrajit, paid it no heed and, laughing, said, "This is nothing at all."
t.6.76.16: Lakṣmaṇa, that bull among men, enraged yet with a fearless face, gathered up dreadful arrows and released them at Rāvaṇi in battle.
t.6.76.18: "Heroes who long for victory do not fight thus in battle!" Speaking to him in this way, he showered him with torrents of arrows.
t.6.76.17: Heroes who have entered battle do not strike like this, O night-wanderer; for these arrows of yours are light and feeble, and even pleasant to bear.
t.6.76.19: Shattered by his arrows, the gold-adorned armour fell apart and scattered over the floor of the chariot, like a net of stars falling from the sky.
t.6.76.20: His armour stripped away by the iron arrows, the valiant Indrajit was covered with wounds in the battle, and he looked like a mountain overgrown with sprouting vegetation.
t.6.76.21: Breathing heavily again and again, the two fought a tumultuous fight in battle, every limb of theirs cut by arrows and drenched in blood on all sides.
t.6.76.22: Those two, the foremost among the knowers of missiles, displaying their missiles again and again, bound together in the sky arrows of every varied form.
t.6.76.23: Shooting flawlessly, swiftly, with wondrous variety and with great skill, both of them, the man and the rākṣasa, waged a tumultuous and terrible battle.
t.6.76.24: The terrible sound of the palm-blows of those two was heard, each one distinct, like that of two very dreadful clouds thundering in the sky.
t.6.76.25: Those gold-feathered arrows, having fallen upon the two bodies in battle, passed right through them smeared with blood and entered the surface of the earth.
t.6.76.26: By the thousands, the arrows of those two clashed in the sky with other well-sharpened weapons, and they shattered and cut one another apart.
t.6.76.27: In that battle the two of them raised a dreadful heap of arrows, like a heap of kuśa grass at a sacrificial session, piled by two blazing fires.
t.6.76.28: The wounded bodies of those two great-souled ones shone forth like a śālmali and a kiṃśuka tree in the forest, stripped of leaves yet covered in blossoms.
t.6.76.29: Indrajit and Lakṣmaṇa, each eager to conquer the other, again and again joined in a tumultuous and terrible clash.
t.6.76.30: In battle Lakṣmaṇa struck Rāvaṇi, and Rāvaṇi too struck Lakṣmaṇa; though the two kept striking each other, they did not grow weary.
t.6.76.31: The two vigorous great heroes, with masses of arrows lodged deep in their bodies, shine like two mountains overgrown with trees.
t.6.76.32: All the limbs of those two, drenched with blood and thickly covered with arrows, shone like blazing fires.
t.6.76.33: Then a long time passed for those two as they fought, yet neither of them turned away from the battle or grew weary.
t.6.76.34: Then, to dispel the battle-weariness of Lakṣmaṇa, who was unconquered at the forefronts of combat, the mighty Vibhīṣaṇa did what was pleasing and beneficial to him; having come into the battle, he took his stand there.
